chunks: Muhammad ibn 'Umayr narrated from Jamil ibn Darrāj who said:
I heard Abā Ja'far (peace be upon him) say: 'When the soul reaches this [place, i.e., the throat], there is no repentance for the knowledgeable, and there is repentance for the ignorant.'
ai.seo_question: What is the difference in repentance between the knowledgeable and the ignorant at the time of death?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Kitab al-Zuhd*, Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) distinguishes between the fate of the knowledgeable and the ignorant at the moment of death, when the soul reaches the throat (*marghama*). The scholarly consensus highlights that the knowledgeable are held to a higher standard of accountability for delaying repentance despite their awareness, whereas the ignorant may receive mercy due to their lack of prior knowledge, though this does not negate the need for eventual understanding.

en.shaykh-tahir-ridha-jaffer: 5.Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Jamīl ibn Darrāj who said, “
I heard Abā Jaʿfar (a) say, ‘When the soul reaches this place (meaning the throat), there is no repentance for the knowledgeable, but there is [a possibility of] repentance for the ignorant.’”
